note: Baseline taken BEFORE deploying the §16.2 work. On this build the org overview has the rollup and streaming but no cache; the project dashboard has none of the three, and still carries the duplicate useAutoRefresh registration.

corpus.shape: concentrated: the events-over-time chart is flat until ~2026-08-16, so 7d and 30d scan nearly the same rows

method: In-page fetch with cache:'no-store', reading response.body chunk by chunk and timestamping each. Navigation timing and paint entries taken from a real navigation. Load generators were running throughout; concurrent ingest is present in every number here.
findings: TTFB and FCP measure nothing on either page: both are ~150-230 ms whether the page streams or not, because Next flushes the document shell before any data is awaited.
LCP is no better: on the overview it lands at 4664 ms against a 4647 ms response end. The largest element is the chart, which arrives last either way.

The chunk arrival profile is the metric that separates them. The dashboard delivers 25% of its bytes at 230 ms and then nothing at all until 21.5 s. The overview delivers 50% by 332 ms and 75% by 3.8 s.
Run-to-run variance on the 30d dashboard is ~12% (19.2 s, 19.8 s, 21.5 s across three runs). Differences below that are noise.
Two back-to-back 30d loads cost the same on both pages, confirming neither has a cache on this build.
Auto-refresh fires twice per tick on the project dashboard. Measured, not inferred: two requests 1-3 ms apart at each tick, ~1.3 s each at the 1h range.
The visibility-aware pause in useAutoRefresh works: a backgrounded tab produced zero ticks in 75 seconds.
The auto-refresh control still renders the "5m" option as "5ms" on this build - the label defect fixed in the branch.

auto_refresh.result: Two full RSC refreshes per tick, 1-3 ms apart, not deduplicated by Next.
auto_refresh.note: Confirms the duplicate useAutoRefresh registration described in the §16.2 streaming commit: DashboardPage called the hook and also rendered DashboardHeader, which renders AutoRefreshControl, which calls it too. At the 1h range each refresh costs ~1.3 s; at 30d each would cost ~19 s.
auto_refresh.caveat: document.hidden was overridden to false to run this. An MCP-driven tab is backgrounded, and the hook correctly pauses on a hidden tab - which is itself a positive finding: the visibility-aware pause works in production. The tick interval is therefore measured from a simulated foreground, and the 25.6 s gap is offset by the visibilitychange resume rather than being a clean 30 s.
auto_refresh.restored: The auto-refresh preference was set back to Off, as found.
